haiku-low.q1: Pages of up to 500 products ordered by id ascending. Requests are strictly sequential, never parallel, so parts cannot be fetched at once.
haiku-low.q2: In sync_state.build_cursor in SQLite. Each page's rows and the cursor update commit in one transaction, so they stay consistent.
haiku-low.q3: A watermark W is read before page 1. Changes after W are replayed from /catalogue/changes since W and applied as idempotent upserts or deletes keyed by id.
haiku-low.q4: The server returns HTTP 410 with resync_required. The client marks the catalogue stale and builds a new generation while the old one stays visible.
haiku-low.q5: It is built as a new build generation beside the active one, then catch-up runs. Promotion sets active_generation to it in a single transaction.
haiku-low.q6: App launch or return to foreground starts it, not Wi-Fi becoming available. It runs at most once every 15 minutes, counted from the last incremental run start.
haiku-low.q7: It re-sends the identical request after waits of 2, 4, 8 and 16 seconds, at most 5 attempts. Then the run stops, keeps saved data, and waits for the next trigger.
haiku-low.q8: It pauses at the current cursor. An in-flight page finishes and is saved, and a failed in-flight request is not retried on cellular. It resumes when Wi-Fi returns.
haiku-low.q9: It applies the record only if its change_seq is at least the stored row's change_seq.
haiku-low.q10: It starts from change_cursor_active. That position moves forward to last_seq after each saved response's changes are applied in a transaction.
haiku-low.q11: It reads products rows stamped with change_seq from one global sequence. Deletes appear as tombstones {id, change_seq, deleted: true}, with rows kept for 7 days.

sonnet.q1: Pages of up to 500 live products (about 1 MB), ordered by id ascending, fetched via after_id cursor (empty for page 1) until has_more is false. Strictly sequential, never parallel.
sonnet.q2: In sync_state.build_cursor (id of last saved product) in local SQLite. Each page's rows are upserted into products under build_generation and build_cursor is set in one transaction, so both commit together or neither does; a killed app rolls back and resumes from the previous page's cursor.
sonnet.q3: Client reads a watermark W (highest committed change_seq) and saves it before fetching page 1. After the last page it replays /catalogue/changes?since=W (catch-up), applying upserts/deletes by id only if incoming change_seq >= stored. Inserts behind the cursor are caught by replay, later deletes removed via tombstones, and tombstones for rows deleted before paging do nothing.
sonnet.q4: The server returns HTTP 410 with code resync_required (since is below the purge floor). On an incremental request, the client sets active_stale = true and starts a full rebuild (step 4), keeping the old catalogue visible. During catch-up, the client discards the build generation and starts a fresh build.
sonnet.q5: A new build generation (highest existing + 1) is built beside the active one, in the same products table, without touching the active one; the download is followed by catch-up. It becomes the one read when step 9 runs in a single transaction setting active_generation = build_generation after catch-up completes. The old generation's rows are then deleted in batches in the background.
sonnet.q6: App launch or return to foreground (Wi-Fi-available does nothing here), when a usable non-stale active catalogue exists, no build is in progress, and at least 15 minutes have passed since last_incremental_run_at (or it is null; a clock moved backwards counts as elapsed). The throttle counts from the start of the last run, whether or not it succeeded. Otherwise it is skipped silently.
sonnet.q7: Re-send the identical request after waits of 2 s, 4 s, 8 s, 16 s, for at most 5 attempts in total. After the 5th failure the run stops, keeps everything already saved, and waits for the next trigger. The attempt counter is in memory only. Page requests are not retried on cellular.
sonnet.q8: Before each page it checks for Wi-Fi; if off Wi-Fi it pauses (step 7) with build_cursor holding the position. A page already in flight is allowed to finish and be saved, then the next check pauses the download. If the in-flight request fails after leaving Wi-Fi, it is not retried on cellular and pauses at the same cursor. It resumes from build_cursor when Wi-Fi returns (Wi-Fi trigger) or on next launch with Wi-Fi.
sonnet.q9: Each change is applied as an upsert (or delete) keyed by id, only if the incoming change_seq is at least the stored row's change_seq; lower change_seq changes are skipped. (Page saves are plain upserts.)
sonnet.q10: It starts from change_cursor_active (requests /catalogue/changes?since=change_cursor_active&limit=1000). The cursor moves forward to last_seq in the same transaction that applies each response's changes, repeating while has_more is true.
sonnet.q11: The change feed reads Postgres products rows with change_seq > since, ordered by change_seq ascending (using the index on products(change_seq)), checked against the stored purge_floor. Deletes appear as tombstones, rows kept with deleted = true, returned as {id, change_seq, deleted: true}.
